scope: Two distinct Phi-3 200-pair run terminations, diagnosed separately.

events.launch_method: foreground child of the agent/SSH session (Bash tool)

timeline.00:33:25 to 00:53:32: no further artifact; baseline monitor was in progress
timeline.expected_baseline_completion: ~01:08 based on run 2's measured 35-minute baseline monitor
timeline.00:53:32: relaunch attempt truncated the original stdout log to 0 bytes
timeline.00:53:36: relaunch rejected by the --fresh guard; its argparse error overwrote the original stderr log

positive_evidence: The process was launched as a foreground child of the agent session, not detached.
The wait command associated with this run returned exit code 137 (SIGKILL).
Background task records for this period were reported orphaned/stopped by the harness.

Controlled contrast: run 2 executed the IDENTICAL command and data, differing only in being launched detached via Start-Process, and survived 8h25m including a full SSH disconnect. Run 1 died within ~20 minutes without a disconnect-independent cause.

ruled_out.host_restart: No System log Kernel-Power 41, 1074 or 6008 events within two days.
ruled_out.application_crash_or_hang: No Application log 1000/1001/1002 events between 00:00 and 01:00.
ruled_out.ram_exhaustion: 127.7 GB physical RAM; the identical run 2 peaked near 19 GB.
ruled_out.cuda_oom: No OOM text in any surviving log, and run 2 completed the same baseline monitor on the same GPU.
ruled_out.python_exception: No traceback in any surviving artifact.
ruled_out.dependency_or_credential_failure: Run 2 started successfully from the same environment two minutes later.

events.why_not_certain: The run's own stdout and stderr were destroyed at 00:53:32/00:53:36 when a relaunch reused the same log paths. The definitive record - exit code and any final traceback - no longer exists. Per the stated policy this is reported as strongly indicated rather than proven.

evidence_destruction_defect.description: Reusing a fixed log filename let a later launch truncate an earlier run's only log.
evidence_destruction_defect.fix: The durable launcher writes to runs/<run_id>/ with a unique run id; log paths are never reused.

evidence: Stop-Process -Id 39632 -Force issued deliberately to free the GPU.
Recorded at the time in results/local_sft200_phi3_seed42_v2/PARTIAL_RUN.json with status PARTIAL_DELIBERATELY_TERMINATED.
Remaining work was two monitor passes at ~7.7 hours each for two data points that could not change the conclusion.

secondary_finding.name: monitor_wall_time_regression_under_vram_pressure

measurement.identical_work: 100 functions x 8 candidates = 800 generations, same model, same panel

secondary_finding.hypothesis: Allocator thrashing once optimizer state pushes the card to ~98% occupancy, so generation cannot obtain KV-cache memory without repeated retry/defragmentation.
secondary_finding.status: UNVERIFIED_HYPOTHESIS - not instrumented. Possibly a fixable defect rather than a property of Phi-3.
secondary_finding.implication: Phi-3 200-pair runs cost about 24.5 hours end to end, of which only ~9 minutes is training. The cost is monitoring, not learning.
